punchline: After nineteen hours awake, people did as badly on an attention test as people who were legally drunk.
thirty_sec: Matthew Walker cites an Australian study: nineteen hours without sleep left healthy adults as impaired as drivers at the legal alcohol limit. Then he looks at young doctors on thirty-hour shifts: 36 percent more serious errors, and far more crashes on the drive home. The worst part is that sleep-deprived people keep insisting they're fine.
